Hi Evelyn / Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement at BrightLane needs to confirm the invoicing cadence and how you plan to run the annual prepay sweep across our EUR & GBP ledgers. Key asks from our side:

- We need an invoice schedule tied to drawdown windows (quarterly triggers preferred).
- Clear ledger tagging so our AP can match against project and country buckets (EUR/UK/ROW).
- VAT routing: we require a short handover pack to send to our tax provider showing which invoices include VAT vs service exports.

Attached is our standard PO template and a sample bank remit. Can you provide a proposed sweep play (high level) and confirm who at Redwood will be the operational contact for month-of-drawdown reconciliations?

PO#: BL-PO-4431

oliver.bennett@brightlane.com
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-jurisdiction prepay sweep & ledger tagging - BrightLane

Oliver — thanks for the clear summary. Below is a pragmatic runbook we can operationalize immediately and attach to the invoice packet. High level first, then operational bullets.

High-level approach
- Annual prepay is invoiced upfront, then funds are swept/allocated to currency-specific ledgers monthly (timed sweep) to align with usage and tax jurisdictions.
- Default sweep cadence: monthly allocation with quarterly drawdown reconciliation windows.
- Ledger tagging: we add two custom invoice tags: project_code and country_bucket (EUR/GBR/ROW). We will provide a mapping CSV that your AP can ingest.

Operational bullets (what we will deliver this week)
- Prepay invoice (initial): one invoice (gross) with metadata fields for VAT applicability per line.
- Allocation CSV: prepay-ledger-template.csv (attached) — includes columns: invoice_id, line_id, project_code, country_bucket, currency, allocated_amount.
- Sweep rules: automated job runs on day 3 of each month to push amounts to ledger buckets; reconciliation report (PDF/CSV) delivered on day 5 of each month to procurement@brightlane.com.
- VAT handover: summary table showing which invoice lines are VAT-charged + Redwood VAT reg number by country. Rishi will own the tax evidence pack for the EU.

Next steps / asks for BrightLane
- Confirm VAT IDs & preferred remit account for EUR/GBP.
- Confirm preferred drawdown windows (we recommend monthly allocation, quarterly reconciliation).
- Approve the attached prepay-ledger-template and the escrow instruction outline so we can attach to the DocuSign envelope.

Attachments: prepay-ledger-template.csv (CSV), Escrow-Instr-BrightLane.pdf (PDF)

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Oliver / team — quick follow-up from finance ops. A few clarifications to make month-of-drawdown processing smooth: 

1) VAT evidence: please send VAT registration numbers for the BrightLane entities receiving invoices (format: country - VAT ID). We will include the VAT flag per invoice line so your tax provider can map easily.
2) Bank remits: if you have separate remits per currency please list them; otherwise we will route to the single remit and tag currency in the allocation CSV.
3) Reconciliation owner: Redwood will run the initial reconciliation and post journals to the ledger; we will send the reconcile CSV + PDF to procurement@brightlane.com and accounting@brightlane.com. Please confirm the accounting email.

Operational note: For draws during UK tax year boundaries we suggest holding cutoffs on the last business day of the month and doing the sweep on the 3rd business day to let FX settle — this avoids late posting into the next tax period.

I'll also coordinate with Rishi for the VAT pack we mentioned.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Billing & Collections
Redwood Inference
